answer.summary: The current task table (schema/current.sql) defines a single table `tasks` with two columns: `id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY` and `title TEXT NOT NULL`. The offline contract query (checks/schema_contract.sql) issues `SELECT id, title FROM tasks LIMIT 0;` — a zero-row read that asserts the table exists and exposes exactly those two columns, without returning or mutating any data. Its stated purpose (per the inline comment) is for a future evaluator to verify the tasks table remains readable. The repository README.md frames the entire fixture as an offline application schema and explicitly forbids applying any migration to live state, which is why the contract check is a pure read assertion against a static fixture rather than a live database probe. The migrations README.md adds that any future schema change requires explicit approval, reinforcing that the contract query guards the current, approved shape of the table against unauthorized drift.
